items.q: By the time the new metro line finally opens, the city ______ on it for eleven years.
items.vi: Đến lúc tuyến metro mới cuối cùng khánh thành, thành phố sẽ thi công tuyến này được mười một năm rồi.
items.explanation: An action continuing up to a future point (by the time … opens + for eleven years) takes the future perfect continuous: will have been working. ✗ will work — simple future, cannot carry the duration for eleven years; ✗ is working — present continuous, no future perspective; ✗ has been working — present perfect measures up to now, not up to a future moment.

items.q: The judge's ______ handling of the case was praised by both sides, neither of which felt it had been favoured.
items.vi: Cách xử lý vụ án công tâm của thẩm phán được cả hai bên khen ngợi, không bên nào cảm thấy mình được thiên vị.
items.explanation: The clue neither … felt it had been favoured means the judge treated both sides equally: impartial (fair, not biased). ✗ indifferent — not caring either way; ✗ apathetic — lacking interest or energy; ✗ aloof — cold and distant in manner. None of those would be praised by both sides.

items.q: When the landlord raised the rent for the third time in a year, it was ______ for the tenants, who began organising a rent strike.
items.vi: Khi chủ nhà tăng tiền thuê lần thứ ba trong một năm, đó là giọt nước tràn ly đối với người thuê, và họ bắt đầu tổ chức đình công tiền nhà.
items.explanation: A third rise that finally triggers a rent strike is the last straw (the final small problem that makes things unbearable). ✗ the last resort — the only remaining option; ✗ the last word — the final say in an argument; ✗ the last laugh — winning in the end after seeming to lose.

items.q: The printing plant was forced to ______ a third of its workforce once the newspaper moved online.
items.vi: Nhà in buộc phải sa thải một phần ba nhân công khi tờ báo chuyển sang phát hành trực tuyến.
items.explanation: Dismissing a third of its workforce because work has dried up is to lay off workers. ✗ lay out — arrange, or spend money; ✗ lay down — put down, or set rules; ✗ lay up — store away, or confine someone to bed with illness.

items.q: ______ the laboratory had repeated the test three times did the researchers announce that the river's lead levels were safe.
items.vi: Mãi đến khi phòng thí nghiệm lặp lại xét nghiệm ba lần, các nhà nghiên cứu mới công bố rằng mức chì trong con sông đã ở ngưỡng an toàn.
items.explanation: The inverted main clause did the researchers announce demands a negative opener: Not until + clause. ✗ Until, ✗ As soon as, ✗ By the time — all ordinary time conjunctions that would need normal word order (the researchers announced); only a negative/restrictive phrase fronted to the sentence triggers inversion.

items.q: The minister sounded distinctly ______ about the bill, praising its aims in one breath and questioning its cost in the next.
items.vi: Bộ trưởng tỏ ra rõ ràng là nước đôi về dự luật, vừa khen mục tiêu của nó ở câu trước lại vừa nghi ngờ chi phí ở câu sau.
items.explanation: Praising … in one breath and questioning … in the next shows mixed feelings: ambivalent (about). ✗ indifferent — not caring at all; ✗ apathetic — lacking interest; ✗ oblivious — unaware, and takes to/of, not about.

items.q: The appeal court ______ the original ruling, rejecting every ground on which the developer had challenged it.
items.vi: Tòa phúc thẩm giữ nguyên phán quyết ban đầu, bác bỏ mọi căn cứ mà chủ đầu tư đã dùng để khiếu nại.
items.explanation: A court that rejects every ground of appeal upholds the original ruling (confirms it). ✗ held up — delayed, or supported physically; ✗ kept up — maintained a pace or standard; ✗ retained — kept possession of, not used of confirming a decision.

items.q: The mayor ______ the report before the press conference; she stumbled over even its most basic figures.
items.vi: Thị trưởng chắc chắn đã không đọc bản báo cáo trước buổi họp báo; bà vấp ngay cả ở những con số cơ bản nhất.
items.explanation: Stumbled over even its most basic figures is evidence she did not read it, so the speaker makes a confident negative deduction: can't have + past participle. ✗ needn't have read — she read it but it was unnecessary; ✗ shouldn't have read — she read it and was wrong to; ✗ mustn't have read — must have is for positive deduction only; the negative is can't have.

items.q: Rather than keep patching the leaking roof every winter, the housing association decided to ______ and replace it entirely.
options: bite off more than it could chew
items.vi: Thay vì cứ vá mái nhà dột mỗi mùa đông, hiệp hội nhà ở quyết định cắn răng chịu đựng và thay toàn bộ mái.
items.explanation: Replacing the roof entirely rather than keep patching is an unpleasant but necessary step: bite the bullet. ✗ bite the dust — fail, die or be defeated; ✗ bite its tongue — stay silent though tempted to speak; ✗ bite off more than it could chew — take on more than it can handle.

items.q: The linguist ______ fieldwork on endangered dialects won last year's prize is now advising the ministry on language policy.
items.vi: Nhà ngôn ngữ học mà công trình điền dã về các phương ngữ đang mai một đã đoạt giải năm ngoái hiện đang cố vấn cho bộ về chính sách ngôn ngữ.
items.explanation: The blank sits before the noun fieldwork, which belongs to the linguist, so the possessive relative whose is needed. ✗ whom — object pronoun, cannot come before a noun; ✗ which — not used for a person; ✗ that — a subject/object relative, leaving fieldwork with no link to the linguist.

items.q: The columnist ______ the nail on the head when she ______ that the city has plenty of homes, just not where people can afford to live.
items.vi: Nhà bình luận đã nói trúng phóc khi bà nhận xét rằng thành phố có thừa nhà ở, chỉ là không ở những nơi người dân đủ tiền sống.
items.explanation: The idiom is hit the nail on the head (say exactly the right thing), and the when-clause needs a finite verb: observed. ✗ struck / observing — strike is not the verb of this idiom, and observing is a participle with no tense; ✗ hit / observing — when she observing has no finite verb; ✗ struck / observed — wrong verb for the idiom.

items.q: Older residents are ______ to abandon the low-rise streets they grew up in, however generous the relocation package.
items.vi: Những cư dân lớn tuổi không muốn rời bỏ những con phố nhà thấp tầng nơi họ lớn lên, dù gói tái định cư có hào phóng đến đâu.
items.explanation: Only loath is followed by to + infinitive: loath to abandon (very unwilling). ✗ averse — takes to + noun/-ing (averse to abandoning); ✗ hostile — hostile to a person or idea, not to + verb; ✗ resistant — resistant to change, again to + noun, not infinitive.

items.q: Rents in the capital have doubled in a decade; ______, wages have barely moved.
items.vi: Tiền thuê nhà ở thủ đô đã tăng gấp đôi trong một thập kỷ; trong khi đó, tiền lương hầu như không nhúc nhích.
items.explanation: Two things over the same decade are set side by side (rents up, wages flat), so meanwhile. ✗ therefore — gives a result, but flat wages are not caused by rising rents; ✗ otherwise — if not, the consequence of not doing something; ✗ likewise — signals similarity, but the two facts contrast.

items.q: Most junior reporters would ______ the chance to cover a general election, even if it meant weeks without a day off.
items.vi: Hầu hết phóng viên trẻ sẽ chớp ngay cơ hội đưa tin về một cuộc tổng tuyển cử, dù phải làm nhiều tuần không nghỉ.
items.explanation: Eager acceptance of the chance (even if it meant weeks without a day off) is jump at. ✗ jump through — jump through hoops, go through tedious procedures; ✗ jump over — literally leap across; ✗ jump off — literally leap down from.

items.q: The committee recommended that the controversial clause ______ from the bill before its second reading.
items.vi: Ủy ban đề nghị điều khoản gây tranh cãi được loại khỏi dự luật trước phiên đọc thứ hai.
items.explanation: After recommend that (also suggest, insist, demand) the verb is subjunctive, the base form: be removed, whatever the tense of recommended. ✗ was removed — past tense, not the base form; ✗ is removed — present, not the base form; ✗ would be removed — modal, not used after recommend that.

items.q: The dictionary's editors keep a ______ eye on social media for words that are slipping into everyday use.
items.vi: Các biên tập viên từ điển theo dõi sát mạng xã hội để tìm những từ đang dần đi vào ngôn ngữ hằng ngày.
items.explanation: Watching carefully is keep a close eye on, a fixed phrase. ✗ tight — goes with grip, rein, budget, not eye; ✗ strict — describes rules or people, not an eye; ✗ near — physical distance, never used with eye on.

items.q: City officials were accused of being ______ about flood risk, insisting the century-old drains would cope as they always had.
items.vi: Giới chức thành phố bị cáo buộc là chủ quan về nguy cơ ngập lụt, khăng khăng rằng hệ thống cống trăm năm tuổi vẫn sẽ chịu được như trước nay.
items.explanation: Insisting the drains would cope as they always had is false confidence that ignores a danger: complacent about. ✗ reluctant — unwilling, and takes to + verb; ✗ apathetic — lacking interest, not over-confident, and takes about/towards only loosely; ✗ averse — opposed, and takes to.

items.q: The developer ______ at the last minute and withdrew its bid for the riverside site, citing 'market uncertainty'.
options: got off on the wrong foot
items.vi: Chủ đầu tư chùn bước vào phút chót và rút hồ sơ đấu thầu khu đất ven sông, viện lý do 'thị trường bất ổn'.
items.explanation: Withdrawing at the last minute is losing your nerve: get cold feet. ✗ got itchy feet — a desire to travel or move on; ✗ got the cold shoulder — was deliberately ignored; ✗ got off on the wrong foot — made a bad start with someone.

items.q: The tenants' association now regrets ______ the landlord's first offer, which looks generous beside the one on the table today.
items.vi: Hiệp hội người thuê nhà giờ hối tiếc vì đã từ chối đề nghị đầu tiên của chủ nhà, đề nghị ấy trông hào phóng hơn hẳn so với đề nghị đang bàn hôm nay.
items.explanation: Regret + -ing looks back at something already done and wished undone: regrets rejecting the first offer. ✗ to reject — regret + to-infinitive only introduces bad news now (we regret to inform you); ✗ reject — regret never takes a bare infinitive; ✗ to be rejecting — continuous infinitive, and still the wrong pattern.

items.q: If the city ______ its drainage system a decade ago, last week's storm would not have flooded three metro stations.
items.vi: Nếu thành phố đã hiện đại hóa hệ thống thoát nước từ một thập kỷ trước, cơn bão tuần rồi đã không làm ngập ba ga metro.
items.explanation: An unreal past condition (a decade ago) with a past result (would not have flooded) is the third conditional: if + past perfect, had modernised. ✗ modernised — past simple gives a second conditional, needing would not flood; ✗ has modernised — present perfect cannot sit with a decade ago; ✗ would have modernised — would belongs in the result clause, not after if.

items.q: Voters grew steadily ______ with a government that promised change every spring and delivered none by autumn.
items.vi: Cử tri ngày càng vỡ mộng với một chính phủ cứ mỗi mùa xuân hứa đổi thay mà đến mùa thu chẳng làm được gì.
items.explanation: Losing faith after being let down (promised change … delivered none) is disillusioned with. ✗ dismissive — treats something as unimportant, and takes of; ✗ disinclined — unwilling, and takes to + verb; ✗ disapproving — thinks something is wrong, and takes of.

items.q: ______ in plain language rather than legal jargon, the new tenancy contract can be understood without a lawyer.
items.vi: Được viết bằng ngôn ngữ giản dị thay vì thuật ngữ pháp lý, hợp đồng thuê nhà mới có thể hiểu được mà không cần luật sư.
items.explanation: The contract is written by someone, so the reduced clause is passive: past participle Written. ✗ Writing — active, would make the contract the writer; ✗ Having written — active perfect participle, same problem; ✗ To write — an infinitive of purpose, which makes no sense here.

items.q: After fourteen hours of talks on the budget, the two parties agreed to ______ and resume in the morning.
items.vi: Sau mười bốn giờ đàm phán về ngân sách, hai đảng đồng ý dừng lại ở đây và tiếp tục vào sáng hôm sau.
items.explanation: Stopping after fourteen hours to resume in the morning is call it a day. ✗ call the shots — be in charge and make the decisions; ✗ call the tune — also be in control; ✗ call a spade a spade — speak bluntly and honestly.

items.q: Had the council ______ with residents from the outset, far fewer of them would ______ opposed the scheme.
items.vi: Nếu hội đồng thành phố thẳng thắn với cư dân ngay từ đầu, thì đã có ít người phản đối dự án hơn nhiều.
items.explanation: Being honest with residents is level with them, and the result clause of a past unreal condition (Had the council …) is would have + past participle. ✗ squared / had — square with means be consistent with, and would had is impossible; ✗ levelled / had — right verb, but would had is not a form; ✗ squared / have — wrong verb.

items.q: The new tram line is expected to ______ pressure on the city's overcrowded northern bus routes.
items.vi: Tuyến tàu điện mới được kỳ vọng sẽ giảm bớt áp lực cho các tuyến xe buýt quá tải ở phía bắc thành phố.
items.explanation: Reducing strain on a service is relieve pressure on, the standard collocation. ✗ release — release pressure is physical, letting gas or steam out; ✗ loosen — goes with grip, rules, a knot, not pressure on; ✗ lighten — goes with a load or the mood, not pressure on.
